claims.statement: Michael Schumacher is a German racing driver.

evidence.locator: Paragraph identifying Germany’s first world champion
Il momento di riprendersi section identifies the driver as German

claims.statement: He was born on 3 January 1969 in Hürth, Germany.
In 1990 Schumacher won the German Formula Three championship and joined Mercedes’ sports-car programme, before entering Formula 1 the following year.
Schumacher raced for Jordan and Benetton in 1991, continued with Benetton through 1995, and drove for Ferrari from 1996 through 2006. After a break, he returned with Mercedes for 2010–2012.
His seven drivers’ world titles came in 1994 and 1995 with Benetton, followed by five consecutive championships with Ferrari from 2000 to 2004.
His Formula 1 debut was with Jordan at Spa in the 1991 Belgian Grand Prix. He returned to the circuit with Benetton in 1992 to take his first Formula 1 win.
On 8 October 2000 at Suzuka, Schumacher secured his first drivers’ title with Ferrari. It ended the team’s wait for a drivers’ champion since Jody Scheckter in 1979.

Paragraph on 2000 and Ferrari’s first champion in 21 years

claims.statement: His Mercedes comeback ended after the 2012 season without another Formula 1 race victory.

Formula 1’s retrospective emphasizes Schumacher’s ability to sustain pace, adapt while driving and give engineers detailed feedback. This is an attributed assessment of his driving, rather than a statistical ranking.

In Mercedes’ account, Toto Wolff credits Schumacher’s technical knowledge, physical preparation and detailed engineering work with helping the team develop. That testimony complements the results record, while remaining the view of a team with which he raced.

evidence.locator: Wolff comments before career chronology and at conclusion.

claims.statement: In the official 2006 drivers’ standings, Fernando Alonso finished first for Renault with 134 points and Schumacher second for Ferrari with 121. The classification records the outcome; it does not establish personal hostility or explain disputed racing incidents.

evidence.locator: Final classification rows 1–2: Alonso/Renault 134 and Schumacher/Ferrari 121
